utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have the appearances for the day, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Carmela Javier and Barney Thomas for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Thomas. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to all. Boris Zorko, Chad Mair, Alex Fielding, Nadia Galinier and Gregor Guy-Smith for Mr. Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. Good morning, Mr. Kodzopeljic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just remind you that -- the witness can't hear any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Just to remind you that you are bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Thank you so much. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There's been discussion between myself and Mr. Thomas, and I think -- well, it would be better probably for Mr. Thomas to say it than I because that way he's going to have to confirm it any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, just to advise you that the MFI status of the exhibits tendered yesterday can be removed and those can be admitted as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I beg your pardon. I will have to say it again my mike was off. All the exhibits that were tendered yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, are you able to check that out for us and make sure that it's done?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. We have 15 MFI from yesterday and they can easily be de-MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. If you would do so. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you so much. If the usher would be so kind as to give the witness the binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kodzopeljic.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yesterday, we were discussing aspects of the special-purpose industry, and I'd like to continue with that particular topic at this point in time. There was a -- I believe it was a factory that Sloboda Cokac [sic] or Kocac [sic], was there not? I'm being --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't think your sentence is complete. You say "I believe it was a factory that Slobodan Cacak."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Cacic [sic].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but what about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was there not. That was it. I believe it's a factory at Slobodan Cacak, was there not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's just that the transcript says, I believe it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Ah, I see. There was. Let me just start the whole thing again and hopefully I'll get the proper pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There was a factory at Cacak, was there not?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it still exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that factory, was that a special-purpose industry factory or was that a military factory?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a special-purpose production factory, and it still operates in the same field nowadays.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to that factory using, for example, do you recall whether or not the manner in which payment was made to the factory or to workers in the factory was based on an estimation of the total number of worker hours or not? For example, what I mean by that, is that factory would engage itself in 10.000 worker hours per month?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the payment was effected on the basis of contracts concluded with the army or someone else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you go ahead lest I forget this question. What is the difference between a military factory and a special-purpose factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we do not make that distinction. It's called the special-purpose factory. It's not called a military factory. You can use it in a colloquial manner, but in official documents and within the system itself it is called the special-purpose production.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The reason I'm asking is because Mr. Guy-Smith asked you if this factory at Cacak was a special-purpose industry factory or a military factory, and you said no, it was a special-purpose production factory. You didn't say what is a military factory or that means one and the same thing. You said no, it is a special purpose. So I thought maybe there is a difference. There is no difference. Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In your answer on page 3, lines 24 and 25, you said: "No, the payment was effected on the payment of contracts concluded with the army or someone else." With regard to the second part of that answer "or someone else," could you identify for us who you mean by "someone else." What people or institutions are you referring to when you say "someone else"?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me to say a few sentences if order to clarify it better.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you could answer my question, and if it needs clarification thereafter, that would be fine. When you say "someone else," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- a special-purpose factory is allowed to conclude contracts locally or abroad with anyone for the purpose of producing items in that factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to this special-purpose factory concluding contracts locally or abroad outside of the army, could you identify for us in your experience those kinds of institutions that the special-purpose industry concluded contracts with, if you know.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember and later on when I worked in that area, they were allowed, for instance, to conclude a contract with the police or with any party involved in All People's Defence, civilian defence, or for that matter with anyone on the market, because this special-purpose factory didn't produce only military equipment. It manufactured other devices as well, because this particular factory had several plants.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the general proposition here as opposed to the specific special-purpose factory that we're referring to, when you indicate that they were allowed to conclude a contract with any party involved in All People's Defence, you introduced a concept that we have heretofore not discussed. Could you tell us what All People's Defence refers to?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. It's a rather broader term, but what I'm talking in particular is that each republic had its own organisation involved in - how shall I put it? - in a system aimed at preparations for potential defence. Within that system they had assets that were actually military assets, and for that particular segment they were allowed to conclude contracts directly with Sloboda.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say that each republic had its own organisation involved in the system -- in a system aimed at preparations for potential defence, are you referring to all of the republics that were part of the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All the republics had their own respective Territorial Defence staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And was that in -- was that in addition to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You've indicated, yes, with the JNA, and my question is slightly different -- different. Was the system of All Peoples Defence that you have discussed that was able to contract with the special-purpose industries a system that existed independently or - and I'll put it that way - independently of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is exactly what I wanted to say. According to regulations governing the special-purpose production, it was laid out how this had to be done. Each factory had an annual production plant and such plant envisaged what the factory was going to do in the following year, and these plants had to be approved by the SSNO and its administration for research, administration, and production which was an integral part of the SSNO, which is the Federal Secretariat for National Defence. So in a way it was still under the supervision of the SSNO and had to be done with their permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: After the break-up of the former Yugoslavia, when the SFRY became the FRY, with regard to this specific issue that we're discussing here in terms of the regulations governing the special-purpose production, was that special-purpose production under the authority of the Ministry of Interior, the Ministry of Defence, the police, the federal government, the army?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The special-purpose production remained under the authority of the Federal Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And after the break-up of the former Yugoslavia when SFRY became FRY. Was there or was there not a division of authority between the army, the VJ, and the MOD? And by that I mean was the VJ subordinated to the SDC and independent of the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that that was the case, but I can't remember the exact time-line, but I know that we were part of the system as you have described it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I just ask a question while Mr. Guy-Smith is sorting himself out. You've just told us that the special-purpose industries were under the authority of the Ministry of Defence, and you did mention this yesterday as well, but yesterday you also at some other stage, and I'm not able to give you the page number now unless I have to search for it, you also said that the special-purpose industry could not sell products to other people or other institutions without your permission. And when you said your permission, I understood you to mean your administration under which you worked. Did I mishear you or did I hear you well?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was precisely the case. I said a minute ago that annual production plans were drawn up for the special-purpose industry. These plans had to be approved by the Ministry of Defence. Now, what was contained in that plan and who the potential clients were going to be depended on what was envisaged in the plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you talked of your administration, are you not -- were you not talking of your administration within the army? I thought -- the impression I've got was that you were saying these special-purpose industries are under the Ministry of Defence and they're not under the army, but as I say, yesterday I thought I heard you say that for them to make these contracts, they've got to do so with the approval of the administration, of which you were a head, in the army. Yesterday, if you will look at page 71 of yesterday's transcript, line 22, it might perhaps be of help. Right. You say if -- I'll start at line 19 of page 71 of yesterday: "As much as I'm able to reply to your question, I don't think any of them concluded any contract directly. I think it all had to go through the SDPR. That is to say, while I was at the head of that department, we didn't conclude a single contract -- or, rather, no factory concluded a single contract with anyone without the consent of my administration or at least its approval." That's -- now, the reason I'm asking you this question is because if you have to give approval for them to conclude a contract, I cannot understand how that happens if they are not under your supervision but they're under the supervision of the Ministry of Defence. Do you understood my problem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. What happened was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would like you -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was due to the fact that I played both roles. So I would like to reiterate and be more specific. When I spoke about the administration, I am talking about the administration that existed when I was assistant minister for military economic activities, and I spoke about myself in that capacity, and not in the capacity of the head of the administration within the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. That's all the explanation I wanted, just to make sure which is which. Okay. Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: A moment ago you mentioned the issue of the annual production plan, and I'd like to take a moment and see if I understand how the annual production plan operated. And perhaps if you could explain it, that would be better than me leading you here, which is could you tell us what is envisioned in the annual production plan for a specific factory?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the Federal Secretariat for National Defence, which later became the Federal Ministry of Defence, there is an administration called -- an administration for research, development, and production, and there's also another administration called the procurement administration. Of course, what we discussed yesterday with regard to the budget, the army and the General Staff specified their requirements and put them forward to the Ministry of Defence for the coming year, and they say that according to the funds available, we would like to procure this and that from the special-purpose industry. So the research, development, and production administration in the Federal Ministry of Defence establishes contacts with special-purpose factories, and tell them that they had been given specific requirements by the General Staff. Therefore, can you tell us and give us a quotation with regard to the capacity that you have for producing the required items. It's a dynamic process. They respond and explain their capacity. So if that is feasible, then the procurement administration concludes contracts for those items for the following year. Other capacities that are insufficient or are rather -- or are, rather, not employed, they intend to employ them to produce items that they would be offering on the market. They also have to do this through co-operation and inform the administration that there were requirements for such products from abroad. So this is how it operated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So if I -- if I understand your answer correctly, there are within the annual production plan two separate and distinct areas in which any given special-purpose industry produces material which is military in nature. One is for -- pursuant to the discussion with the MOD, and the Ministry of Defence's determination of what the requirements are, and the other is what I'm going to call generically the private sector, which could include institutions, other armies, other nation states.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's how it worked, but their involvement in production for other states and other army nevertheless had to be effected through the Ministry of Defence -- or, rather, the SDPR. However when, it came to the civilian sector, it was up to them to conclude independent contracts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I want to see if you will confirm or not, since you've talked about special-purpose industries, whether or not the following rules apply.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if we could have on the screen 3372D. And just if -- we need to look at the first page in both languages and then we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. We don't have the first page in English, so let me ask you this question: Could you, looking at the B/C/S part of the screen, tell us what that says. What is it?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "This rule on military institutions which operate on the principle of obtaining and division of revenues."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if we could go to B/C/S pages 29 -- first of all, if we go to B/C/S page 23. And with regard to one of the issues that we have been speaking about generally, looking at the bottom of the page, which is circled, it says -- that's Article 90, and is that the rule with regard to how gross income is to be determined?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this applies to merely institutions which base their business on generating and distributing income. This is not special-purpose industry. These are overhaul [realtime transcript read in error "overall"] institutions that we discussed yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. And with regard to Article 90, I note that it has the term "JNA" here in section number 1. Was the same rule used when the JNA transformed into the VJ or were there different rules that were used at that time?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same rule and the same instructions applied containing the same postulates.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And those postulates are: "The total gross is verified from charged income by the institution from: "1. Realisation of products, services and goods for the needs of," and I'm going to put in here the generically army. "2. By purchasing products, goods and services on domestic and foreign markets." Right? That's what it says?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right. You're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Heeding the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Apologies for the interruption, Your Honour. There's just a mistake in the transcript at page 11, line 23. I think that should be a reference to "overhaul institutions" not "overall institutions."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thomas. I was wondering what that refers to. Even overhaul I still don't understand, but anyway. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Heeding the Court's previous admonition, we can take this document off the screen at this time since I've read the entirety of the language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. May we remove -- the document may be removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, could you do us a kindness of explaining the differences between what we've just discussed in the special-purpose industry?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand your question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My question is is the same formulation used with the special-purpose industry as was used in Article 90 that we just discussed? Or was there a different formulation?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The procedure was very similar. The technology of the procedure was very similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you say the technology of the procedure was very similar I'm at a bit of a loss in terms of what you mean by the technology of the procedure. If you could be of some assistance there?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did try a minute ago to explain in that a company which is supposed to draw its plans for the next year, and if that company performs within the special-purpose industry, receives a task from the Ministry of Defence which is based on the requirements of the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you. Perhaps the difficulty we're having is with the word "technology." The use of that word in that particular -- in that particular answer, I think, was causing -- was causing me some difficulty. I would -- I probably would have used another word or perhaps its translation. We understood your answer previously. But now that the President has a look of query on his face, so I'm going to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought your question still was you want to know from the witness how the total gross is verified from -- for purposes of special-purpose industries.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is an excellent way of putting the question that I want to get, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you said the difference --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- he didn't know what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Taking Judge Moloto's question and adopting it with his permission, could you tell us whether or not the article that we just read, Article 90, is the same manner in which the total gross is verified for purpose of the special-purpose industry or was a different methodology used?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will repeat. The principle was not identical but it was similar. Firstly, plans are drawn based on the requirements of the army, and then when it comes to the other elements --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm going to interrupt you, sir. We understand that. That is the plan of production. How is gross income verified? Do you -- for purpose of special-purpose industries, do you verify it by what has been sold minus what has been purchased, you know? As Article 90 says. Article 90 is telling us how you verify gross income is cost of sales minus -- or from where -- what is sold finally. Am I confusing you further?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm an engineer and I have problem with finances and how financial plans are drawn. For example, I want to produce a hundred tanks. I conclude a contract with the authorities as to how many tanks they're going to finance, and they pay me, and what I receive I spend on production materials, electricity, salaries and all of the other costs that are incurred within the production process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How do you -- how do you then determine your gross profit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not very well-versed in finances. However, I assume that in the course of the production if I don't use all the materials, if I don't use all the money for the salaries, whatever costs that I've -- that I've had I deduct from what has been contracted and that's my profit. Maybe our systems differ. In my system workers' payments are also costs. Maybe in your system it's different. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We're not talking systems -- different systems here. All we want to know what happened in the former Yugoslavia. You see, Article 90 that we looked at just now told us how gross profit is determined for overhaul industries. Mr. Guy-Smith wants to know how the same thing was determined for special-purpose industries. You say the principle is similar but you articulate it differently from where it stands in Article 90. This is the reason we are having this discussion, because we're trying to clarify how gross profit was determined for special-purpose industries and how differently that was from Article 90, which is for overall industries. If you do know. If you don't know -- as you say, you're an engineer, sorry, you don't know, and you can just tell us you don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me say I don't know then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Kodzopeljic. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Perfectly fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I will take note of your proclamation you're an engineer and adjust some of our discussion accordingly. Were you ever made aware in 1994 of the Supreme Defence Council deciding to organise foreign trade in weapons and military equipment through one state-owned enterprise under the absolute control of the federal government and the Federal Ministry of Defence? Were you ever made aware of whether that happened --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: That's a leading question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He can say, yes, I was made aware of it or I wasn't aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: That makes it a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, here we go into the argument of that was leading or not. I'll put it -- I can ask: To your knowledge did the Supreme Defence Council ever conclude that they would organise foreign trade in weapons and military equipment through one state-owned enterprise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do apologise, Your Honour. I was rephrasing the question. I was taking his comment into mind. I was trying to rephrase the question. You're right, there was an objection. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All right. Okay. If you want to rephrase, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did the supreme council --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Defence council.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Supreme Defence Council in 1994 ever conclude that they would organise foreign trade in weapons and military equipment through one state-owned enterprise under the control of the federal government and the Federal Ministry of Defence. And if you are, that's fine, and if you're not, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that decision, but I do know that that company has existed for 30 or 40 years now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's not my question, and you've answered it by saying you're not aware of the decision and I thank you. I'd like to move back now to the area of material lists, and before we go into any specific material lists, one of the things that we were discussing yesterday was material lists and accounting and the relationship between the accounting departments and the material lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if we could have D384. And I'm going to be going to B/C/S page 10, and my understanding is that the English is 1D12-0549.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, what I'd like you to do -- can you see the screen or do you need to have it a little bit larger?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has to be a bit larger, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I'm focusing -- I'm going to be focusing your attention on Articles 80, 81 initially. And I'd just like you to take a quick glance at Article 80 and 81, if you could. And if you could tell us when you've finished reviewing the document.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. With regard to Article 80, is this one of the articles that regulated this particular issue, and by that I mean the issue of material accounting documentation?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to Article 81, if you could specifically take a look down towards the bottom part of the page. There are a series of numbers that discuss what each material accounting document -- and here it says obligatory contains, and after that there are some eight requirements. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is all spelled out very correctly and very precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to those eight requirements, are the requirements that are contained in Article 81 requirements under which -- under which the various institutions had to operate as regards the informations to be contained in any accounting document?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could go to Article 85, both in the B/C/S and in the English. And in the B/C/S I think we're going to have to move to the next page, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And if we can enlarge the English a little bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: First of all, just to make sure that we're on the same page, if you could tell me what the heading is before we reach Article 85. What does -- what does that say in Serbian?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "1.1 Material List."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And looking at Article 85, going down 1, 2, 3, paragraphs, I note that there is a form number which is MP-20. Is that the form that we were discussing yesterday?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. MP-20. This MP stands for material business transactions, and we discussed it yesterday, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe you explained to us that's what MP stood for yesterday. And there are a series of -- a series of -- what seem to be requirements under 1 and 2. Could you take a look at that in -- in Article 85, that deal with both the sender and the receiver.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to -- with regard to this particular article, is this the article that guided and ruled the sending and receiving of material and what was required with -- with the list that was accompanying that material?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is how things were regulated, and other situations concerning property and goods were regulated by this. In any case, this regulates what senders are supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And anyone else apart from senders?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And those who received goods and material and all those within their authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could now take a look at Article 87.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You'll have to go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to -- I see. Article 87 is on two pages, so you -- the beginning of Article 87 is on -- is at the bottom of this page in the lower right-hand side. If you just take a quick look at that, and when you've finished reading it, if we could move over to the second page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I'd like you to, if you could, focus your attention on the second paragraph for a moment. And does this paragraph describe the manner of approval, certification, and recordation with regard to material?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And finally, Article 88.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yesterday we were talking about copies and white copies and blue copies and pink copies, and I don't know whether we did terribly well in that regard in terms of making things clear to the Chamber, but with regard to the rules and regulations contained in Article 88, are these the rules that apply to the manner in which material lists for sending, for receiving, and for recordation are to be followed?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the very last sentence of Article 88 -- and I just want to make sure that we have the same translation. Could you tell us what the very last sentence in the second paragraph says in Article 88.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Material lists of the sender and the recipient are combined and archived together."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would move the admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: It's a matter that could easily be rectified, sir, but at the moment I have a relevance objection. We just need to know that these rules were in force in the FRY during the period of the indictment as opposed to being applicable at any other period.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were these rules applied and in force in the FRY during the -- during 1993, through and including the end of your tenure?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe the relevant articles did not bear the same number, but the rules were very similar. Maybe you don't understand what the "Military Official Gazette" is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Why don't you tell us?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All regulations published by the military were published in a gazette called the "Official Military Gazette," and everybody was duty-bound to refer to it and to use it. All amendments were also publicised and defined once they were published in the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the information and requirements that are contained in the document that we've been discussing, is it my understanding that of those requirements and that information is something that was substantially similar? utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that these regulations were 100 per cent identical, but when it comes to the issue of material lists specifically, I can say that this regulation was completely identical. There was no difference both in terms of substance and the subject of the regulation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I move the document's admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number -- I beg your pardon. It is already admitted. It is D384.

utterances.text: Well, then, we were fighting over something that didn't need to be fought about.

utterances.text: When you asked for it to come on the screen, you called it by the -- by its exhibit number, D384.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the question of whether or not you had full and complete information concerning preparation of your budget, is the question of who sends and who receives any particular item of importance to you? Yesterday, at page 12280, the following question was asked and the following answer was given: "Q. With regard to the issue that we were discussing earlier, that being the issue of planning the budget, what importance, if any, do the material lists have with regard to those plans?" Answer commencing on line 12: "A. The material lists are important and on the basis of these lists the officer in charge drawing up a plan knows exactly what he has at his disposal, knows what's coming according to norms applicable to each unit and to each type of asset, and on the basis of that he can be able to draw up plans for the next year or for the next five-year period as the financial plans were usually made for." So I would take issue with Mr. Thomas's position.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I note the time, Your Honours. I wonder if I could just have a moment to consider that. I'll discuss the matter with my learned friend, and we can have an agreed position.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I apologise for going over the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We will take a break and come back at quarter to. Court adjourned.

utterances.text: We've had a discussion. I think we've come to an agreement. I'm going to -- I'm going to venture a question and hope that the question ventured is the agreement we've made. I think it is.

utterances.text: Okay. I see Mr. Thomas is smiling, so I take that as an agreement.

utterances.text: Going back to box number 4, reviewing the information that is contained in box number 4, what difficulties, if any, does the information that is contained on this exhibit cause for purposes of your planning?

utterances.text: Very well. I'm not going to focus on some other areas in this particular exhibit, but I would like to ask you one question, which is going to box number 23. There are two entries. utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there's no information.

utterances.text: I would note, Your Honours, that in the English copy the number "1" is inserted into the English copy. I don't know where that information comes from. utterances.text: Noted. There is something else I also do note, that in -- in the box number 28, in the English there is 1.936, which I don't see in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And in the B/C/S there is a number 50, which I don't see in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would agree with you entirely. So obviously there's some difficulties in terms of where this -- where the information came from in the English copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And where the information went to from the -- the 50 from the B/C/S copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, if it's of any assistance, plainly there has been some error in transcription. The Prosecution accepts that what should be in the English version is that 1 shouldn't be there, and instead of the 1.936, there should be a 50 in column number 28. That's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any comment, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No comment at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could have now on the screen P574.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, I would like to go down to the bottom of this form before we remove it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I note that -- if we can scroll up the B/C/S, please, a little bit. Sorry. Can you move it the opposite direction first? Okay. Scroll it up. Now, I don't see anything in boxes 37, 38, and 39.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In both the B/C/S and in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.text: So I would have expected that an official of the General Staff of the VJ should have signed there as the sender.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Assuming that the information is correct in box number 4, that one can assume that the General Staff, then one would think that that would be signed by someone at the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So --

utterances.text: I think this presents a series of difficulties in terms of what the exhibit actually stands for and how it can be relied upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then who --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I just think there are a series of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm just making observations --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- factual observations at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Absolutely. Understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I don't see the signature of the sender or even his or her stamp, the stamp that I see here, if one looks at the signed part, it looks like there's a stamp of the recipient.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's my -- that would be my best understanding of what we have -- what we have been told, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would you confirm that, Mr. Thomas?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct. We have no signature or stamp for the sender. We have the signature and stamp of the receiver.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Okay. Now you called for what else, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe I called for --

utterances.text: In 574, I'd like to focus your attention on the upper left-hand corner of the document. And if you could confirm for us -- once we get the B/C/S.

utterances.text: I don't have the B/C/S yet.

utterances.text: Looking at -- looking at your copy in the binder, I'm going to be directing, and I'll just tell you where I'm going to be directing your attention. utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I take it that your answer would be the same with regard to the information that's contained in box number 4 here that you gave us in terms of P572.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]

utterances.text: If we could go to 575. We take that off the screen and go to the next document, which is P575.

utterances.text: Now, with regard to this particular document, once again let's start with box number 4. Does -- does that box contain information which causes difficulty in planning or does not cause difficulty in planning?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is enough information there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And going to the bottom of the document on the left-hand side. I note there seems to be evidence of some stamp, a part of stamp which is legible, and there is a name contained in this particular document in box number 38; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.text: Now, I'd like to go back just for a moment. Could you -- to box number 4. Could you tell us what you can see in the B/C/S version of box number 4, what it says?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What I didn't understand and I would now like to understand is what do you mean, sir, it is not correct? What is wrong with it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. And was that the mistake also with the previous document, that it didn't have a 12-digit number? Thank you. At least now I understand what you mean by it's incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to this particular exhibit, you had discussed the issue of a stamp for the -- a received stamp. There were two stamps at the bottom of the document. Does this document have a stamp upon it in B/C/S? The B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we now see P576.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Once again I'm going to be focusing your attention -- perfect. utterances.text: Yes, you're right. Ah, we're talking about Bogutovacka Banja. That's the only difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to this document, I take it that your answer would be the same as with regard to the previous documents that this causes you difficulty in terms of planning.

utterances.text: Yes. It's impossible to know what this is about.

utterances.text: And I'm now going to the bottom of the document, if we could. I see that this document, I believe, suffers from some of the same infirmities that you referred to before, which is that there's no entry with regard to box number 32, 37, 38, and 39, and there is no stamp.

utterances.text: You are right.

utterances.text: Now, with regard to box number 29, after the entry of "296," do you see any entry in that box? Is there any writing at all within that box?

utterances.text: With regard to --

utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.text: That's accepted, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] You mean box 36?

utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.text: And I think that as a matter of fact, with regard to 36 it indicates signed by someone, but I'm not arguing or asking for any comment with regard to that particular issue.

utterances.text: No. I see that. My learned friend is right. I would accept that boxes 40 and 41 don't contain any entry.

utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.text: And with regard to signatures in those boxes, what was the purpose for those signatures?

utterances.text: And finally with regard to this particular exhibit of the plaintiff, I note there is no stamp in the area where -- concerning these boxes, boxes 40, 41, on the right-hand side. Would you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirm that.

utterances.text: Thank you. If we could now see P580.

utterances.text: Thank you. Okay.

utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.text: If we could have that document taken off the screen and the next document, which is P580.

utterances.text: With regard to the information that is contained in box number 24, would you confirm that there are no nomenclature numbers of any sort for those entries?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that.

utterances.text: With regard to the bottom on the left hand, would you confirm, as you have previously with regard to boxes 32, 37, 38, 39, there is no information entered, nor is there a stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is no information. I can confirm that.

utterances.text: With regard to box number 14, a box that we spoke about on the previous document, it has some information. As I understand it, what it says is the "Drina Corps Command."

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirm that.

utterances.text: Is there contained therein any address as to where that -- where the receiver, the Drina Corps Command, was located?

utterances.text: No.

utterances.text: If you know, with regard to logistic material, would logistic material be kept at the location of the Drina Corps Command wherever that may be? And "wherever," I mean in terms of an address.

utterances.text: Well, it will have to be specified very precisely to which depot it is going or to which logistical unit it's going.

utterances.text: Okay. And when you say "depot" or "logistical unit," is -- that's something, I take it, that's distinct from the Drina Corps Command itself.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would -- I'd note --

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only have "PCS," which is abbreviation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would note for the record that the English Exhibit P580 has inserted there a number 2, which does not exist on the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: That's accepted, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could go to --

utterances.text: Just before you go to --

utterances.text: Thank you. If we could have the next exhibit, which is P581.

utterances.text: In box 6 there's a date. Sender Ladjevci VK --

utterances.text: Mr. Kodzopeljic, I don't know if you had an opportunity to hear the translator. Because you are reading, usually when we read we speed up, so if you could slow down, please, so the translator can hear what you say. If you can repeat what you just said, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll repeat. So box number 6, the date is 22/11/93. Next to it it says: "Senders VKC, 2895 Ladjevci." Then in box number 7, "302." In number 8, "21," and in box 11, "Ladjevci." This is what I have on my copy.

utterances.text: I understand, and I believe that's also what we have on our copy.

utterances.text: Except that the number 21 is in box 9 in the English, not box 8. I think also in the -- in the B/C/S.

utterances.text: I think it's also in box 9 on the B/C/S, Your Honour. I think he may have misspoken. With regard to --

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. It's box number 9.

utterances.text: With regard to the information contained in box number 4, what -- what information do you have there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, from 1993 to 1999; the 2nd of April of that year I was the chief of the technical administration of the logistics sector of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia. In other words, the Chief of the General Staff was my second-ranking superior. As of the 2nd of April, 1990 [as interpreted], until the moment I was pensioned off, I was the assistant federal minister for defence in charge of military economic activities. That institution was under the authority of the Ministry of Defence, and the Ministry of Defence was part of the government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Judge David, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: I would like also to find out what kind of connections, interrelations, these two functions had between the two, and especially if in the functions in the army you had any orientation, control, supervision on any one or some of them of these special-purpose military industry. And at any rate, what kind of supervision, control, orientation, direction you had in the army over the special-purpose industries.

utterances.text: If I might, Your Honour, I understand your question conceptually. utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.text: Independent of the conceptional issue that you're raising, so I just want to make sure that we have the right dates here.

utterances.text: Absolutely. I think that starting at 1993, you said that in this answer that -- let me go back to your answer. "In other words, the chief of the General Staff was my second-ranking superior. As of the 2nd April 1990, until the moment I was pensioned off, I was the assistant federal minister for defence in charge of military economic activities. utterances.text: I understand your question entirely, and once again I have no problems with it conceptually. utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: I have not put any kind of limit in time, but the witness himself has answered specifically on dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's what my concern is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: And so I just wanted the answer not from your comments, but I just wanted to clarify by the witness himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Once again I have absolutely no difficulty whatsoever with what you're seeking to understand. I'm just trying to be clear with regard to that one aspect of the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Let's ask the witness about the dates. I would like very much you to, Witness, to clarify on the time, the dates, you know. I ask you a question. You answer that. You could say it is the same answer, it's a different answer, I don't know, as Judge Moloto always said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I -- thank you very much. I don't know, Your Honour. I may have misspoken. The date is 2nd April 1999, and if I mentioned the year 1990, it's my mistake. I misspoke. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: So, Witness, during the year 1993 and on, you had no dual functions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.text: And during the time that you had this function in the army, could you precise exactly the dates in which you had that function in the army? Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From 1993 up to the 2nd of April, 1999. I was the chief of the technical administration of the logistics sector, and my second ranking in command was the Chief of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The additional question: During that time, from 1993 up to the 2nd April 1999, had you, as part of your function, any direction, orientation, supervision, control, participation on the production of this special industries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, never. I did not have any authority over them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: So in the description of your functions, there were nothing that imply a supervision or any orientation as to the special-purpose industries. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely nothing. There was nothing in my job description with regard to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to look at the right-hand side of this document, if I could, please. Focus your attention on number 14, and could you tell us what's indicated there.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I have here is "30.KC."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know what that signifies?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. The 30th Personnel Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the nomenclature number in box number 24, do we have one?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are just the first four digits.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And with regard to the issue of the category and year of production, are there any entries in box number 26 with regard to the category and year of production?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This does not exist in my copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would note for purposes of the record that with regard to Plaintiff's P588, there is the insertion of the number "01" on the English copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: That's accepted, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Going to the bottom of the document, looking at the left-hand side -- I guess we're going to have to go once again over to page 2 in the English. Okay. With that having been done so the Chamber has the benefit of taking a look at the English translation, looking at the document in B/C/S would you confirm that there is a stamp and a signature in boxes 37 and 38?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two signatures and a stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And above that, in the body of the area where there is information concerning the nomenclature and type of supplies, there's also another stamp. Do you see that stamp? And there's a signature.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As you're looking at that right now, can you tell us what the significance of that is?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Received 2.000 --" sorry, "268 boxes or crates," and a date, 18th of June, and I don't see the -- and I believe that there is also an indication of the time when those were received, at 1700 hours. If you want me to explain, the ammunition was packed in crates or boxes, and for this type of ammunition those boxes contain up to twenty hundred eight rounds, and I believe that the figure 268 refers to the packaging of the ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you for that. Could you look at box number 41 on the lower right-hand side, please. Box number 41 is a box where the manager is supposed to sign; is that correct? The receiving manager.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And what are the responsibilities of a receiving manager, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it a manager or a handler? You said a manager, and I suppose you meant handler or shop steward. Which do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I meant whoever the person who is supposed to sign in box 41 is. I have it translated as "Manager." Perhaps I'm using the wrong word. So I'm just going to box -- all I'm doing is going to box number 41. What are the responsibilities of the individual who should sign in box number 41, if you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a person, a man who is directly charged with the materiel specified in the documents that he had. In other words, if there is a depot, nobody can enter that depot without his approval. If he's absent, he takes the depot keys with him so that nobody can get in while he's absent.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Looking at box number 41 on this document, is there any entry in that box?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in here. The only thing we can see is the title, "Handler."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would note for the record that with regard to Plaintiff's 588, in the English version of this exhibit there is inserted the following: "/?SGV/."

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: That's accepted, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I wish you all a good day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you wish us a good day, could we go back to the first page of this document in both languages. Could you -- if it's possible at all to enlarge a little bit the B/C/S, because I would like Mr. Kodzopeljic to see something. Can you go -- move to the left, please. No, to the left. The opposite direction. No, no, no. To the left. And can you bring it back. Still go up. Right. And go more to the -- or you can't go any further. Mr. Kodzopeljic, on the top right-hand corner of the B/C/S there is a word that looks like "Obrasac" or "Obrazac" which doesn't appear on the English. Are you able to tell us what that might mean.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, yesterday we already discussed that. The word stands for "Form," and what should follow is "MP-20." It's one of the forms from that set of instructions about bookkeeping and accounting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Forgive me for my forget fullness. But just by way of a comment, you see that 03591158 next to that word which again looks like an ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are thanked most heartily by me. We are supposed to stop now for the day.
